correctness.rationale: The stated formula and prime specialization are correct. At 2m lines, Bézout forces a disjoint partition into trisecants. The rational flex gives the zero-sum group law for distinct points; summing over the partition contradicts the unique nonzero involution. The Skolem positions give a partition of [1,3m] into triples (j,m+a_j,m+b_j) with the first two terms adding to the third. For each triple not containing h=3m, taking both signed orientations covers its six distinct signed residues. The remaining residues are exactly 0,h,±a,±b with a+b=h and 0<a,b<h, a≠b. The three stated zero-sum triples have distinct entries and cover these residues. This also works for m=1 (triples {3,1,2}, {3,5,4}, {0,1,5} modulo 6). Each triple yields a rational line. In the prime family p≥5, the cubic is smooth with a flex at infinity, cubing permutes the field, the character sum vanishes, and there is just one nonzero rational two-torsion point. In the invariant-factor decomposition the smaller factor divides gcd(p−1,p+1)=2 and cannot be 2 with this two-torsion. The congruences on m=(p+1)/6 follow, and both prime classes are reduced modulo 24. The supplied verify.py was inspected, not executed. Its frozen checks are bounded examples, not the basis of the quantified conclusion; the review relies on the symbolic proof and classical Skolem existence.
